summary:
We developed MARS-X, an aerospace-grade astronaut spatial operating system combining an augmented reality helmet HUD, an interactive 3D Mars GIS engine, and an autonomous AI copilot. Built with Three.js and real NASA JPL MOLA elevation and USGS datasets, it delivers immersive first-person surface exploration across 50 Martian locations, including Jezero and Gale craters.

Mars surface exploration carries severe risks: communications latency up to 22 minutes, disorienting terrain, extreme cryogenic cold, and blinding dust devil vortices. MARS-X solves this with terrain-conforming AR navigation chevrons, a tactical hazard-avoidance minimap, and computer vision slope safety classification. An integrated offline AI voice copilot continuously monitors suit life-support telemetry (oxygen, pressure, radiation) while narrating historic NASA rover science.

MARS-X is critical because future crewed interplanetary expeditions demand total operational autonomy. By transforming raw planetary satellite data into actionable, real-time visual and vocal navigation, MARS-X bridges life-or-death survival intelligence with scientific discovery—empowering astronauts to navigate, avoid hazards, and explore Mars safely.
